name: NAMIBIA

flag.title: Flag of Namibia
flag.note: Sun, blue, red & green diagonal bands

lead: Namibia is on Africa's south-west coast, where orange dunes meet the cold Atlantic. It has the world's oldest desert and Earth's darkest skies. Few people live here, so elephants, oryx and ancient rock art have lots of space.
geo: The Namib Desert runs along the Atlantic coast. Its red-orange dunes at Sossusvlei reach 325 metres tall. A cold ocean current brings fog to the beach.
Inland, rocky highlands give way to the thorny Kalahari. In the north, Etosha Pan is a giant salt flat. Few clouds keep the sky ink-dark, perfect for stargazing.
animals: Namibia has about 3,000 free-roaming cheetahs. Elephants, black rhinos and lions visit Etosha's waterholes. One Skeleton Coast beach has 100,000 seals.
Sociable weavers build the world's largest bird nests. Hundreds of birds share one haystack nest. African wild dogs hunt in packs.
culture: Namibia has eleven national languages. The Himba of the north coat their hair in red ochre paste. It shields them from the sun.
Food mixes African and German flavours. Windhoek serves kapana (grilled street meat) and bratwurst. Thumb pianos, drums and throat singing make the music.
history: The San people have lived here for 20,000+ years. Germany took the land in the 1880s. From 1904 to 1908 German forces killed around 80,000 Herero and Nama people.
South Africa then ruled for 75 years. SWAPO's struggle won independence on 21 March 1990. Germany apologised for the killings in 2021.
wows: The Namib Desert is about 55 million years old, the oldest on Earth.
Dune Big Daddy is roughly 325 m tall, about as high as the Eiffel Tower.
Namibia was the first country to protect nature in its constitution, in 1990.
Whale bones and fog-wrecked ships gave the Skeleton Coast its name.
About 3,000 cheetahs roam free here, more than in any other country.
Fish River Canyon is Africa's largest, 160 km long and 550 m deep.
About 10% of the world's diamonds come from the seabed off Namibia.

myths.fact: Not always. Antarctica is the biggest desert on Earth. A desert is just a place with very little rain.
The north has summer rains every year. Even the Namib blooms with flowers after a rare shower.
